source: Seeded from archaeology plan, Realmz source anchors, Divinity guide line references, and existing generated coverage docs.

targets.why: Realmz source now maps Data ED3 to 40-byte Extra Action Point script rows loaded by loaddoor2(id), with callable roots for direct opcode 39, EDCD branch fields, opcode 7 action-data patching source rows, Global hooks, battle macros, monster death macros, timed encounters, random rectangles, hidden encounter button paths, and door items that store an Extra Action Point row in item sp5. Providence's semantic import now promotes EDCD branch link kinds, opcode 7 copy-source rows, negative battle macros, random rectangle doors, timed doors, and door-item macro links; remaining work is default UI terminology, validation polish, and safe fixed-row authoring.

Realmz source now anchors the top-level loadextracode opcode table, including opcode 39 as direct ED3, opcode 7 as action-data patching that loads an Extra Action Point source row before copying its script slots, opcode 8 as same-map Action Point copy rather than an EDCD or Extra AP call, the added shapes for opcodes 19/40/51/55/64/106, opcode 13 as Action Point percent mutation rather than an Extra AP call, opcode 92 as a two-row random-rectangle shape mutation using ID and ID+1, opcode 122 as message+sound fumble parameters with preserved unused fields, opcode 37 as movement/heading rather than sound/message, opcode-specific battle fields for 2/48/56/107, opcode 2's dual-use sound-or-revived-loss-Extra-AP field, absolute-value message targets for damage/heal opcodes 15/16, source-backed sound fields for condition/spawn opcodes 43/124, signed count/test fields for opcodes 30/65/74, and opcode 86 split from opcode 87 because its branch mode lives in a different EDCD field. The one-based/zero-based/force branch-mode conventions now decide whether EDCD targets are Extra AP, simple encounters, complex encounters, or messages.

Realmz source proves Data SD2 and Data OD text storage. Providence compiles fresh/authored rows semantically and preserves unchanged legacy padding or noncanonical capacity only through the compatibility annex. The Divinity Strings Sound field has no central Realmz message-storage consumer; sounds belong to caller records unless binary evidence proves a separate Divinity-only write path.
